input: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

results_vs_guidance.claim: Original Q1 FY2027 guidance: revenue $545–565 million, adjusted EBITDA $135–145 million, gross margin approximately 57%, and ending paid Connected Fitness subscriptions of 2.455–2.475 million.

Q1 FY2027, ended September 30: revenue $559 million, $4 million above guidance midpoint; adjusted EBITDA $168 million; gross margin 61.3%, versus 57% guidance; free cash flow $143 million. Connected Fitness subscriptions ended at 2.475 million, the top of guidance.
Seeking Alpha's earnings feed reported GAAP EPS of $0.19 beating estimates by $0.08, and revenue of $559.2 million beating by $7.04 million. It reported Q2 revenue consensus of $635.55 million.

Consensus discrepancy: SGB instead reported EPS consensus of $0.08 and revenue consensus of $554.55 million, versus actual EPS of $0.19 and revenue of $559.2 million. Both opened feeds show a beat, but their estimate sets are not reconciled.

Current Q2 FY2027 guidance: revenue $625–650 million, adjusted EBITDA $85–100 million, gross margin approximately 50%, and ending paid Connected Fitness subscriptions of 2.425–2.445 million. Revenue declines approximately 3% year over year at midpoint.
FY2027 guidance remained unchanged: revenue $2.30–2.40 billion, adjusted EBITDA $475–525 million, gross margin approximately 54%, and free cash flow of at least $350 million.

credit_signals.claim: Peloton launched a proposed $600 million senior-secured note offering, described by the issuer as due in 2032, alongside a proposed $200 million five-year revolver. Proceeds plus cash would repay remaining term loans. The announcement did not establish completed financing or a final coupon.

S&P assigned a BB- issuer rating with stable outlook and BB ratings to the proposed debt. Its report describes the notes as due in 2031, conflicting with the issuer's 2032 description; final maturity requires reconciliation.

Cash and equivalents were $1,342.2 million at September 30, 2026. Following a $280 million post-quarter term-loan repayment, Peloton reported gross principal debt of $1.048 billion, rounded—not a debt-free balance sheet.

Before the proposed refinancing, the existing term loan and revolver mature May 30, 2029; $350 million of 5.50% convertible notes mature December 1, 2029. These are contractual maturities, not confirmed dates for closing the new financing.

The existing $100 million revolver was undrawn, so financial covenants did not require testing. When revolving borrowings are outstanding, disclosed tests include $250 million minimum liquidity and $1.2 billion trailing-four-quarter subscription revenue.

missing_fields: catalysts: confirmed next earnings date, NEC post-trial ruling date, and an exact international Tread Flex launch date within November 10, 2026–May 10, 2027 were not verified.
credit_signals: final refinancing coupon, pricing/closing date and reconciled note maturity were not verified; issuer and S&P maturity descriptions conflict.
event_driven: Skōp purchase consideration and fresh activist, equity-buyback, tender-offer, spin-off or strategic-review disclosures were not verified.
alternative_signals: current hiring/headcount, newer layoffs, and named commercial contract wins or losses were not verified.
insider_and_ownership: open-market insider purchases and notable recent fund increases or reductions were not established by the opened filings.
results_vs_guidance: a reconciled, provider-independent consensus comparison was not verified.
output.research_view: As of November 10, 2026, Peloton is a cash-generation and deleveraging case rather than a proven subscriber-growth recovery: Q1 beat company guidance, but subscriptions contracted and full-year guidance was unchanged. The immediate focus is pricing and execution of the proposed refinancing, followed by holiday treadmill demand as the October 2025 subscription-price increase annualizes. Normalize tariff and recall benefits before valuing earnings, and treat the conflicting consensus feeds and proposed-debt maturity disclosures cautiously.

event_driven.claim: Peloton confirmed completion of its acquisition of Skōp, an early Connected Pilates innovator, to support differentiated products and experiences. Purchase consideration was not verified in the opened announcement.

catalysts.claim: An October 2 trade report schedules expiry of the U.S. member-only treadmill promotion for 11:59 p.m. ET. This is a near-term pricing/demand checkpoint, not a confirmed earnings catalyst; no later extension was verified.

Virtual annual meeting at 11:00 a.m. ET: director election, auditor ratification and executive-compensation vote-frequency proposal. This is a confirmed governance date, rather than an announced strategic-transaction vote.

risks.claim: Subscriber erosion remains material: at September 30, Connected Fitness subscriptions were 2.475 million, down 9% year over year; average monthly churn was 1.7%, up 10 basis points year over year. Cash-flow improvement has not established subscriber growth.

Earnings quality: management identified approximately $25 million of combined tariff- and recall-related Q1 favorability. Treating the entire quarterly beat as recurring operating improvement would be aggressive.

The NEC patent case produced a $20.5 million damages award for direct infringement. The court expressly labeled this judgment non-final; the award should not be confused with a fully resolved litigation outcome.

The latest quarterly filing says NEC sought ongoing royalties and/or a permanent injunction, while Peloton challenged findings through post-trial motions. Briefing finished October 20, 2026; no decision date was verified.

Governance concentration: the proxy reports TCV-affiliated entities with 42.6% of total voting power. Class B shares carry 20 votes versus one for Class A, limiting outside Class A investors' influence.

alternative_signals.claim: Historical workforce action: Peloton cut roughly 11% of employees, primarily affecting engineering teams, according to the February 2 trade report citing Bloomberg and company confirmation. This is not evidence of a new November layoff round.
Peloton opened commercial-operator orders for its Commercial Bike and Commercial Tread. Order availability is verified; named customer wins and contracted revenue were not established.

Reported member promotion: Tread Flex discounted from $2,195 to $1,995 and Tread+ Vision from $6,695 to $5,295, with discounts reaching $1,400. These are the trade report's dated promotional prices, not independently reconfirmed November transaction prices.

Management said Q1 was the final quarter compared with the period before the October 2025 subscription-price increase; the increase begins annualizing midway through Q2 FY2027, reducing that comparison tailwind.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig sold 10,000 Class A shares at $5.45. The Form 4 says the sale followed a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted September 2, 2025; it was not an unplanned contemporaneous sale.
COO Charles Peter Kirol's Form 4 reports 28,849 shares disposed at $5.33, but the footnote identifies shares withheld for taxes on vested RSUs—not discretionary open-market selling.

Vanguard Portfolio Management's signed Schedule 13G reports 24,549,783 shares, or 5.88%, as of June 30, 2026, held for ordinary-course investment rather than control. This is a dated ownership snapshot, not a verified new purchase.

Nantahala Capital Management's Schedule 13G amendment reports 21,547,895 shares, or 5.17%, as of June 30, 2026, with an ordinary-course investment certification. The opened filing does not establish the size of a recent position change.

The proxy ownership table reports BlackRock with 58,215,193 Class A shares, or 13.5%, using information from its June 4, 2026 Schedule 13G/A. This is the proxy's disclosed snapshot, not a current trading-flow signal.
